codeReview.summary: The queue pagination regression test is solid, but the restaurant-switch proof does not actually verify the reset behavior it claims. The implementation only adds tests in `OpsEmailDeliveryClient.test.tsx`; no runtime code changed.

issues.description: The restaurant-switch regression test never proves that tab/filter/page state resets or that data reloads under the new restaurant context. `renderClient()` hard-codes `initialRestaurantId="rest-1"`, so after selecting the second restaurant the client immediately syncs the URL back to `restaurantId=rest-1` before any new fetch occurs. The assertions then expect `getRestaurantEmailDeliveryFeed` and `getRestaurantEmailDeliverySummary` to remain at one call, which is the opposite of the requested 'reload under the new restaurant context' behavior. This means the added proof can pass even if restaurant switching is broken, so requirement (2) remains uncovered.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `fullstack-worker` skill still mandates browser verification even for test-only tasks. This worker correctly skipped agent-browser for a pure regression-test change and recorded a deviation, suggesting the skill should explicitly allow test-only work to omit browser checks.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/skills/fullstack-worker/SKILL.md step 7 requires agent-browser for all tasks, while the handoff `skillFeedback` for worker session `55e766ed-d851-42c8-a250-83b211c23e59` documents skipping browser verification because only tests changed.

summary: Review failed: the queue-page reset proof is valid, but the restaurant-switch proof is ineffective because it asserts no new restaurant-scoped fetches happen after switching restaurants, which contradicts the feature requirement and can mask a broken reset flow.
